findings.title: Stale normal dataplane result mutates a newer route
findings.summary: A stale generation-1 dataplane success can be matched against the current generation-2 route entry. FRR logs the sequence mismatch but continues into the success path, marking the current route installed, updating FIB/NHT state, and enqueueing owner notification work while the kernel still reflects the older route. Scenario 3 reproduces the same root cause through an NHT-facing invariant after the stale result creates an inconsistent RNH snapshot.

findings.title: Late async route notify mutates the current selected route without generation gating
findings.summary: A late `DPLANE_OP_ROUTE_NOTIFY` can be processed after a newer route generation becomes the selected FIB route. The async notify path matches by prefix/type/instance and lacks a route generation or sequence gate, so it can update FIB/offload/NHT state on the current route from a stale notification context. This can make route owners or NHT clients observe stale realization state.

findings.title: BGP suppress-fib pending can survive ZAPI route send failure with no outstanding work
findings.summary: BGP sets `BGP_NODE_FIB_INSTALL_PENDING` before the queued Zebra route announcement is actually sent. If the later ZAPI send returns `ZCLIENT_SEND_FAILURE`, the queued inode is released and no Zebra route, dataplane operation, or owner notification remains outstanding. The pending flag is normally cleared by a route-owner installed/fail notification, so this path can leave BGP suppressing advertisement indefinitely.
